:::: {.poster-grid}

::: {.col}

::: {.card title="Motivation" accent="blue"}
Are two quantum measurements **compatible**, i.e. can they be performed jointly? Answering this in general requires full **process tomography** followed by a **semidefinite feasibility test**, with a cost that grows rapidly with the Hilbert-space dimension $d$.

The **quantum SWITCH** offers a shortcut: applying two measurement processes in a coherent superposition of causal orders turns incompatibility into a **single interference signal** on a control qubit, with a sample complexity **independent of $d$**.
:::

::: {.card title="The SWITCH as an incompatibility witness" accent="blue"}
::: {.placeholder height="16cm"}
Fig. 1 — Quantum SWITCH circuit: control qubit $\lvert +\rangle$, two processes $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ in superposed orders, Fourier measurement of the control.
:::

With the control in $\lvert +\rangle$ and measured in the Fourier basis, the probability of the "$-$" outcome is

$$
p_- = \tfrac{1}{4}\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{Tr}\left(\rho\,\lvert[C_i,D_j]\rvert^2\right),
\qquad
\mathrm{NCOM}_\rho = \sqrt{2p_-}.
$$

For projective observables with spectral projectors $\{P_i\}$, $\{Q_j\}$ the Lüders channels are dephasings, and the signal equals the **mutual eigenspace disturbance**

$$
\mathrm{MED}_\rho(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) = \sqrt{1-\operatorname{Re}\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{Tr}\left[\rho\,P_iQ_jP_iQ_j\right]}.
$$

::: {.keybox}
**Key point.** For sharp observables, $\mathrm{NCOM}_\rho = \mathrm{MED}_\rho$: one interference fringe certifies incompatibility, with no tomography and no SDP.
:::
:::

:::

::: {.col}

::: {.card title="A time-bin quantum SWITCH" accent="coral"}
Instead of two spatially separated interferometer arms, the control is a **time-bin qubit** $\{\lvert e\rangle,\lvert l\rangle\}$:
the early bin experiences [$\mathcal{A}$ then $\mathcal{B}$]{.ab}, the late bin [$\mathcal{B}$ then $\mathcal{A}$]{.ba}.

::: {.placeholder height="15cm"}
Fig. 2 — Optical setup: heralded polarization qubit, time-bin control, waveplates + calcite crystals for each block, final interference on the control.
:::
:::

::: {.card title="Dephasing via birefringent walk-off" accent="coral"}
A birefringent crystal delays $\lvert V\rangle$ relative to $\lvert H\rangle$ by $\Delta\tau = L\,\Delta n_g/c$. Tracing out the temporal mode multiplies the coherence by

$$
\gamma(\Delta\tau) = \int \lvert f(\omega)\rvert^2 e^{-i\omega\Delta\tau}\,d\omega \;\longrightarrow\; 0
\quad (\Delta\tau \gg \tau_{\text{coh}}),
$$

realising the Lüders dephasing $\mathcal{A}(\rho)=\sum_i P_i\rho P_i$. A **QWP + HWP** pair rotates the dephasing axis to **any** measurement basis.

::: {.note accent="coral"}
**Timescale hierarchy:** $\tau_{\text{coh}} = 3.3\,\text{ps} \ll \Delta\tau_A \approx 10\,\text{ps},\ \Delta\tau_B \approx 18\,\text{ps} \ll \Delta t_c = 150\,\text{ns}$
:::
:::

::: {.card title="Robust by construction" accent="coral"}
Temporal shifts commute, $T_{\tau_A}T_{\tau_B} = T_{\tau_B}T_{\tau_A}$, so both causal orders produce **identical output wavepackets**, regardless of crystal lengths.

::: {.keybox}
**No active interferometric stabilization needed:** the two orders recombine coherently by symmetry.
:::
:::

:::

::: {.card title="Outlook: unsharp measurements" accent="gold"}
For **POVMs**, commutativity is *no longer necessary* for joint measurability. The operational meaning of the switch signal must therefore be established anew. We are developing the theory of what the SWITCH certifies in this regime.
:::
